specs.anchorText: A kernel that responds to a bright region moving rightward across three frames is detecting rightward motion
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a small, friendly cartoon cube character with curious eyes and tiny arms slides through a short stack of three transparent cartoon photo frames arranged front to back like a flipbook. Inside the frames a bright dot shifts a little to the right from the first frame to the last. As the cube character peeks through all three frames at once it grins and points at the shifting dot, having just spotted the motion. A friendly 2D flat square character watches from one single frame nearby, looking slightly jealous. Soft warm oranges for the cube, soft blues for the frames, expressive and gentle, generous margins. XKCD-inspired textbook style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on one cube spanning several frames to catch motion.
specs.alt: A cartoon cube character sliding through three stacked transparent video frames at once, spotting a bright dot that shifts rightward across the frames, while a flat 2D square character confined to a single frame looks on, illustrating how a 3D convolution kernel sees motion that a 2D kernel cannot.
specs.caption: Slide the same little window across stacked frames instead of one, and an edge in space becomes motion in spacetime.

The bottom lane is a narrow, skinny conveyor carrying many small, simple frames zipping by fast, pulled by a tiny nimble lightweight robot (the fast, thin pathway). A few small connector pipes link the fast lane up into the slow lane. The two lanes merge into a single friendly robot holding up a label tag. Soft blues for the slow lane, warm oranges for the fast lane, expressive and clean, generous margins. XKCD-inspired textbook style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on one wide-slow and one thin-fast pathway merging.
specs.alt: Two parallel cartoon conveyor pathways merging: a wide slow lane carrying a few large detailed frames pulled by a heavy robot for appearance, and a thin fast lane carrying many small frames pulled by a tiny nimble robot for motion, with connectors feeding the fast lane into the slow one, illustrating the SlowFast spatial-versus-temporal budget split.
specs.caption: Appearance needs many channels but few frames; motion needs many frames but few channels, so pay for each separately.

specs.alt: A cartoon robot repeatedly redrawing a field of motion arrows while consulting a giant all-pairs lookup table on the wall, with a loop arrow and a stack of progressively sharper arrow maps, illustrating how RAFT encodes features, correlates every pixel pair, and iteratively refines the flow estimate.
specs.caption: A hard guess about where everything moved is easier made as many small, repeated corrections than as one giant leap.

specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: two cartoon pedestrians, one wearing a red scarf and one wearing a blue hat, walk toward each other and cross paths in the middle of the scene where their tracking boxes overlap. A small, slightly flustered tracker robot stands nearby holding two numbered identity tags and, at the moment of crossing, accidentally hands the red person's tag to the blue person and vice versa, looking confused. The overlapping boxes are drawn around the pair at the crossing point. Soft blues and warm oranges, gentle and good-natured humor, never mean, generous margins. XKCD-inspired textbook style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on the moment two identities get swapped as the people cross.
specs.alt: Two cartoon pedestrians crossing paths with overlapping tracking boxes while a flustered tracker robot accidentally swaps their numbered identity tags, illustrating the dreaded ID switch that happens when motion prediction alone cannot tell two crossing objects apart and which a learned appearance embedding fixes.
specs.caption: When two paths cross and the boxes overlap, a motion-only tracker swaps who is who; appearance is what re-binds the right identity.
